No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Africa Energy Bank Takes Off With Helmy Ghazi As Pioneer President by Nse Anthony-Uko 1 minute ago in Business Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The $5 billion Africa Energy Bank (AEB) has formally commenced operations, with Egyptian banker Helmy Ghazi appointed as its pioneer president. The launch followed the bank’s inaugural General Assembly in Abuja on Saturday, October 31, 2026, and was announced by Afreximbank and the African Petroleum Producers’ Organisation (APPO).
At the meeting, the General Assembly appointed Ghazi as president and constituted the bank’s first Board of Directors. The board includes representatives from the public and private sectors, as well as leading policy institutions across Africa.
The AEB is structured as an independent, supranational, pan-African financial institution with $5 billion in authorised capital. It will mobilise funding from governments, national oil companies, financial institutions and private investors to support energy development across the continent.
The bank is expected to finance oil and gas production, power generation, transmission infrastructure, refining, storage and distribution projects. It will also support investments linked to emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, which requires reliable and scalable energy supply.
Its backers say the institution will help address Africa’s estimated $200 billion energy investment need. The AEB is also expected to support a “just energy transition,” enabling African countries to develop their energy resources while expanding electricity access and industrial capacity.
Ghazi previously served as Deputy CEO and Managing Director, Head of Global Banking, at HSBC Bank Egypt. He has more than 25 years of banking experience, with expertise in customer growth, risk management, team development and international markets.
His immediate task will be to operationalise the bank, strengthen its governance and investment framework, attract additional capital, and begin financing viable energy projects across Africa.
The launch comes as traditional financiers increasingly withdraw from fossil-fuel projects, despite the continuing importance of oil and gas to many African economies. The AEB is expected to help fill that financing gap and strengthen Africa’s energy security.
